findings.title: remove_member uses group.users.delete, bypassing GroupUser callbacks and the user_count counter cache
findings.body: `remove_member` deletes the membership with `group.users.delete(user_id)`. For a `has_many :through` association with no `:dependent` option, Rails deletes the join rows with `delete_all`, so no `GroupUser` destroy callbacks run and the `counter_cache: "user_count"` on `GroupUser#group` is never decremented. Consequences: the `user_count` column (rendered by `BasicGroupSerializer` and shown in the admin group list and `userCountDisplay`) stays stale/too high forever, and the per-membership cleanup normally done on destroy (e.g. clearing a granted group title / primary group) is skipped. The existing `Group#remove(user)` helper (which destroys the `GroupUser` record) should be used instead.

findings.title: remove_member raises RecordNotFound (500) when user_id is not a member of the group
findings.body: `group.users.delete(params.require(:user_id).to_i)` passes an Integer to the collection proxy, which internally calls `find` scoped to the association. If the id does not belong to the group (already removed, bogus id, double-click on the remove button, or `to_i` turning a non-numeric value into 0), `ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound` is raised and the admin gets an unhandled error instead of a graceful response. The action should look the user up explicitly and no-op / return a proper error when the user is not a member.

findings.title: create silently drops alias_level sent by the client
findings.body: `Discourse.Group#asJSON` (app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js) always includes `alias_level`, and `create` POSTs that payload, but `Admin::GroupsController#create` only assigns `name` and `visible`. An admin who picks an alias level while creating a new group has that choice silently discarded (the server keeps the default), while the client model still shows the chosen value, so the UI and database disagree until the next save. `update` handles `alias_level`; `create` should too.

findings.title: members endpoint does not validate limit/offset, allowing 500s and unbounded queries
findings.body: `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `offset = params[:offset].to_i` are used directly in `limit(limit).offset(offset)` on a publicly reachable endpoint. A negative value (`?offset=-1` or `?limit=-1`) produces `OFFSET -1` / `LIMIT -1`, which PostgreSQL rejects ("OFFSET must not be negative"), turning user input into a 500 error. A huge value (`?limit=1000000`) makes the server load and serialize every group member in one request, an easy resource-exhaustion vector. Both parameters should be clamped (e.g. limit between 1 and some max, offset >= 0).

findings.title: Breaking change to the public /groups/:name/members.json response shape
findings.body: The endpoint previously returned a bare JSON array of serialized group users; it now returns `{members: [...], meta: {total, limit, offset}}`. This is a public, unversioned endpoint used by third-party clients and plugins (and previously returned all members for non-automatic groups, now a default page of 50). Any existing consumer iterating the array will break with no deprecation path. If this change is intended, it should be called out in the PR description/release notes so integrators can adapt.

findings.title: No spec coverage for the rewritten members endpoint
findings.body: `GroupsController#members` changed both its response format (array -> `{members:, meta:}`) and its paging semantics (always paginated, default limit 50), yet only `spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb` was updated in this PR. `spec/controllers/groups_controller_spec.rb` is untouched, so existing assertions about the old array response are likely broken, and the new behaviour (meta.total, limit/offset handling, ordering) has no test at all.

findings.title: totalPages off-by-one produces an extra empty page
findings.body: `totalPages` is computed as `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`. When `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit` this returns one page too many: with 100 members and limit 50 it reports 3 pages, and clicking "next" twice lands on offset 100 where the server returns no members, so the admin sees an empty member list and a bogus "3/3" indicator. It should be `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)` (with the 0 case handled), and the `next` action should clamp offset to `(totalPages - 1) * limit` rather than to `user_count`.

findings.title: addMembers/removeMember swallow server errors with no user feedback
findings.body: `addMembers` and `removeMember` only attach a success handler (`.then(function(){ self.findMembers(); })`) and the calling controller actions (`addMembers`, `removeMember` in admin-group.js.es6) ignore the returned promise. If the request fails - e.g. the 422 `can_not_modify_automatic` response, a validation error, or any 500 - nothing is displayed and the member list is not refreshed, so the admin believes the operation succeeded. Note the server also silently ignores unknown usernames in `add_members`, which compounds the lack of feedback. A failure handler showing `bootbox.alert` (as `save`/`destroy` do) is needed.

findings.title: findMembers returns undefined instead of a promise when the group has no name
findings.body: The early return was changed from `Ember.RSVP.resolve([])` to a bare `return;`. `findMembers` is otherwise promise-returning and is chained by callers (`actions.next`/`actions.previous` return its value, and plugins/other code may call `.then` on it). For a group without a name the function now returns `undefined`, so any `.then()` on the result throws a TypeError. Return a resolved promise to keep the contract consistent.

findings.title: Public group members page is now silently capped at 50 members with no pagination
findings.body: The public group page iterates `members`, which `group-members.js.es6` populates via `model.findMembers()` using the model's default `limit: 50` / `offset: 0`. Previously the endpoint returned all members for non-automatic groups, so the full list was shown. There is no next/previous control in this template (only the admin template got one), so for any group with more than 50 members the page now shows a truncated list with no indication that members are missing, while the counts endpoint still reports the real total.

findings.title: remove_member spec issues a PUT while the route only accepts DELETE
findings.body: The "cannot remove members from automatic groups" example calls `xhr :put, :remove_member, ...`, but `config/routes.rb` maps only `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"`. Controller specs dispatch directly to the action and ignore the HTTP verb, so the test passes while never exercising the real routing; a verb regression in routes.rb would go undetected. Use `:delete` as the other removal example does.

findings.title: Removal spec asserts association count but not the cached user_count
findings.body: "is able to remove a member" only checks `group.users.count == 0`, which is a live SQL count and therefore passes even though `group.users.delete(user_id)` skips the `GroupUser` destroy callbacks and leaves the cached `user_count` column at 1. Asserting `group.user_count` (the value exposed by `BasicGroupSerializer` and shown in the admin UI) would catch the stale-counter bug introduced by the new `remove_member` implementation.

findings.title: add_members assumes the usernames param is a String
findings.body: `usernames = params.require(:usernames)` followed by `usernames.split(",")` raises `NoMethodError` (500) if a client sends `usernames[]=a&usernames[]=b`, which is a natural way to call this endpoint and is what Rails produces for an array parameter. Accept both forms (e.g. `Array(usernames).flat_map { |u| u.to_s.split(',') }`) or validate the type and return a 400.
